'''Jonathan V Sweedler''' (born 1961) is an American [[chemist]] specializing in bioanalytical chemistry, neurochemistry and cell to cell biology and behavior.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.neurochem.su.se/om-oss/neurokemiseminarier/professor-jonathan-v-sweedler-neurokemiseminarium-1.343926 |title=Neurokemiseminarium |date=August 31, 2017 |publisher=su.se |accessdate=October 8, 2017}}</ref> He is the James R. Eiszner Family Endowed Chair in Chemistry at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://chemistry.illinois.edu/directory/profile/jsweedle |title=Jonathan V. Sweedler, Chemistry at Illinois |date=December 20, 2017 |publisher=illinois.edu |accessdate=December 20, 2017}}</ref> Additionally, he holds a faculty appointment in the Beckman Institute.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jonathan V. Sweedler |url=https://chemistry.illinois.edu/jsweedle |website=Chemistry at Illinois |accessdate=November 2, 2019}}</ref> Sweedler is a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]. He is also an Elected Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]], for which he acts as the Editor in Chief of the journal ''[[Analytical Chemistry (journal)|Analytical Chemistry]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=-ZAnHfYAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Jonathan V. Sweedler|publisher=October 7, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pubs.acs.org/page/ancham/profile.html|title=Jonathan V. Sweedler|publisher=acs.org|accessdate=October 8, 2017}}</ref>

He previously served as director of the School of Chemical Sciences at UIUC, and as director of the Roy J. Carver Biotechnology Center (University of Illinois), where he was involved in the genome sequencing of several organisms. Currently his laboratory has facilities in the [[Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology]] and the [[Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology]] at the University of Illinois. His research has led to the discovery of several mammalian neuropeptides.

Serving as the chair of dissertation committees at the University of Illinois, he has graduated approximately 60 students with PhD degrees. As of 2019 his publication record includes over 400 journal articles, with an [[h-index]] estimated to be in the 60s or 70s.<ref>(based on citations in the Google Scholar and Web of Science databases)</ref>

==Education==
He graduated with a [[B.S.]] in chemistry from the [[University of California, Davis]] in 1983 and a [[PhD]] from the [[University of Arizona]] in 1989.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.scs.illinois.edu/sweedler/Sweedler.html |title=Jonathan V. Sweedler |publisher=illinois.edu |accessdate=October 8, 2017}}</ref> Thereafter, he was an NSF Postdoctoral Fellow at [[Stanford University]] with [[Richard Zare]] (chemist) and [[Richard Scheller]] (neuroscientist) before joining the faculty at the University of Illinois in 1991.
